# Autocomply AI presents Coffee and Compliance with guests Harmonic Security

- Channel: Autocomply AI

## Description

AI Risk, Governance, and Compliance in 2026: Trust, Verification, and Continuous Monitoring

We sit down with Ed and James from Harmonic Security as we take a look at how AI tooling is being adopted quickly, and the pace of change is creating a growing gap between what an organisation believes is under control and what is actually happening in day-to-day operations. Tools are entering environments through standard routes such as integrations and approvals, but also through unauthorised use, including personal subscriptions and ad hoc uploads of company documents into AI services. This creates exposure that leadership and assurance functions may not have visibility into, even though obligations to customers remain constant.

Recent incidents have intensified scrutiny on third-party risk and assurance. Allegations of invalid SOC 2 certifications and the downstream impact on third parties, subprocessors, and “subprocessors of subprocessors” highlight how quickly risk can propagate when trust is misplaced. The issue is not limited to a single incident; it reflects broader pressure in the market to obtain certifications quickly as a route to enterprise sales.

# AI Security

- Channel: Trust in Digital Life

- Published: 2026-02-24T12:30:00-08:00
- Category: People & Blogs
- Language: en

## Description

AI security is a significant issue in AI systems development and adoption. It is also a tool supporting both defenders and attackers. From AI-assisted cyber-attacks to data exfiltration, in attacks on critical infrastructure and in support of widespread fraud, AI security has become a top issue. The panellists discussed AI security attacks, LLM-specific threats and the latest developments in this area as well as AI’s use by defenders in protection of critical infrastructure, improving evidence of issues and detecting attacks better and earlier than is possible without AI.

The panel of eminent speakers were:

- Roderick Kaleho, Agentic AI & Security Consultant, LogicRiver
- Jason Martin, Director, Adversarial Research, HiddenLayer
- Matthew Rosenquist, Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), cybersecurity strategist and founder of Cybersecurity Insights
- Marcel Winandy, Senior Expert Cyber Security Architect, E.ON Digital Technology
- Rupert Young, Chief Product Officer, Maxmind

The session was moderated by TDL strategic advisor, Claire Vishik.

# Webinar: Evaluating Wind and Solar Power Plant Harmonics Against IEEE Harmonic Standards

- Channel: Energy Systems Integration Group
- Length: 01:03:23
- Views: 2.1K
- Language: en

## Description

Featured Speaker: David Mueller, Director of Power System Studies, EnerNex

Webinar Abstract: This webinar will provide an overview of the topic of harmonics from wind and solar power plants. Transmission system operators are increasingly vigilant to check the harmonic emissions from wind and solar plants during energization. The process has been confusing because there are multiple standards. Some plants have seen delayed energization due to concerns for harmonics. IEEE 519 is the original harmonic standard, but it was primarily developed for load equipment. It has very strict provisions, but leaves room for interpretation. IEEE 1547 has been developed and recently modified for distributed generation on distribution systems, but is not directly applicable to larger plants on the transmission system. IEEE P2800 is currently being drafted to address harmonics from the larger plants connected to the bulk electric system. The webinar will address these various standards, and will provide a summary of some of the practices in other countries.
